title: Routed experts of any size against the device: placed, cached and computed by a decision tree
description: One plugin for a mixture of experts larger than the device. The model plugin calls the experts slot as for experts that fit: begin(layers, experts, format, hidden, inter, device_bytes) once, load() per expert, open() after its own pools, forward(layer, x, ids, weights, rows=None, prompt=None) per routed layer. The plugin decides the tier (every expert on the device; a mapped bundle store in host memory behind a device expert cache in every byte left; a store file on disk read on the host when host memory does not hold them), who computes a miss (the CPU tier in the device's bits, while the link copies the missed expert into the cache beside the round so it serves from the next one, in the slot of the expert routed longest ago; or, where the CPU tier cannot compute them, every miss copied over the link before its layer reads it, with the device's rows in the kernel's tensor arithmetic), and how prompt chunks run (their misses staged through the cache's ring). Its facts say what it decided and why; its telemetry carries a one-line diagnosis. Experts a GGUF checkpoint stores (format gguf: each layer's formats as the file has them, IQ1_S to Q8_0, Q2_0 included) are cached and streamed as their stored bytes and computed by crit's gguf-rows kernel in the slots they are in; the CPU tier computes their misses in gguf-rows' declared order on the host (in torch, outside a capture). Inside it: device-expert-cache's ExpertCache, expert-tensors' BundleStore, host-expert-tier's CpuTier and heterogeneous-expert-dispatch's DeviceDispatch, grouped-experts' kernel.

tier.description: where the routed experts live: auto decides at begin() (device when they fit beside the model's device_bytes and the margin, ram when host memory holds them beside ram_headroom_mib, else disk)

misses.description: who serves a decode miss: cpu, the CPU tier computes every miss beside the device while the link copies it into the cache beside the round (where the tier and its in-stream join build here); link, every miss copied over the link before its layer reads it, every expert then on the tensor cores; auto, whichever serves a missed expert sooner on this machine, timed at load (the CPU tier where it takes under four fifths of the link's time)

policy.description: the cache's residency beside the CPU tier: recent, every miss copied in beside the round and serving from the next, in the slot of the expert routed longest ago (what is resident is what was routed last); ranked, decayed route counts ranked at round boundaries and the top keys swapped in. Over the link the clock picks each miss's slot

keep_routes.description: 0: every route. N: each token keeps the router's first N routes and the rest are left out (not renormalized), in every tier and for decode rows and prompt chunks alike. An approximation of the model that trades quality for fewer expert rows and fewer misses; it is the same for a row whatever the cache holds, so replies stay repeatable and independent of the requests beside them. For quality mode speed, where the run's drift budget judges it; never in preserve

approximates.what: each token keeps the router's first N routes and drops the rest (not renormalized): every layer's expert output changes, decode and prompt rows alike

swaps.description: recent: the most misses one round copies into the cache (the slots listed at its start); ranked: the most experts one boundary swaps in (four times as many after a topic change). Their copies read host memory beside the CPU tier

swap_period.description: ranked policy: rounds between swap boundaries

fill_blocks.description: thread blocks of the cache's fill kernel (the copies beside the round read host memory by SM loads): too few and a round waits for its copies at its end (4 measured 18.6 ms a round against 16.7 at 32 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's experts, RTX 5090), more change nothing; 0: the cache's default

side_swaps.description: ranked policy: copy a boundary's swapped bundles on a side stream beside the round (joined at its end, mapped by the next round) instead of in the round's own stream before its first layer; recent copies beside the round always

prompt_arithmetic.description: a prompt chunk's rows when the CPU computes decode misses: auto (the default), the faster arithmetic that keeps the level the engine's configuration asks of its prompt rows (exactness, docs/PLUGINS.md#exactness): tensor where it asks repeatable or row-exact, declared where it asks exact, declared or nothing; declared, the CPU's integer order (the decode rows' bits: exact honesty, slower prefill); tensor, the kernel's tensor cores (for an engine that asks repeatable or row-exact prompt rows). With misses over the link every row is the tensor arithmetic

reserve_mib.description: device memory open() leaves free past the model's pools: a fixed cache's whole reserve for the model's prompt temporaries, graphs and workspaces; an elastic cache's until the engine's warm requests ran

elastic.description: the cache's slots in an elastic range (crit_plugins.memory, the driver's virtual memory API): address space for every expert, backed for what open() finds free less reserve_mib, then for every free byte the device does not keep (the run's VRAM headroom and a short prompt's room: crit_plugins.memory's headroom, which Core's loader sets), with every slot's address fixed; prompt steps get their room from it through the device's step frames. Off, or where the API is not reachable, the cache keeps its size from open()

ram_headroom_mib.description: host memory left free when begin() decides whether the experts fit in host memory

host_tier_mib.description: the disk tier's host tier: host memory that keeps the experts the device cache evicts, each expert held once (in a cache slot or here), with the store file read past the OS's page cache at a queue depth. -1: what host memory has free beside ram_headroom_mib when begin() runs; 0: none, the page cache holds what was read

store_dir.description: a folder for the bundle store file (built once per checkpoint and layout, reopened without the loads after); empty: the host's plugin cache where it gives one (context.cache: crit run gives every run one; one store a checkpoint there, keyed by the package's plugin code too, kept only on a local disk with twice its size free), else anonymous host memory, built at every load (the disk tier needs a file)

store_path.description: an existing complete bundle store file of this checkpoint and layout (its index beside it), opened as it is and never rebuilt; a store that does not match is refused

profile.description: a residency profile in the package (device-expert-cache's residency_profile.py, or a routing profile save_profile() wrote) the cache starts from when no profile_save file exists yet

pinned.description: the pinned core, for a host short of memory: this share of the cache's slots at open() holds the experts the profile option's file ranks hottest for good (no plan evicts them, no shrink gives them back), and the store leaves them out of host memory, read once from the store file straight to the device: each of them is in one place. Needs misses: cpu, the recent policy, a profile and a store file (store_dir or store_path); 0: none. The slots left follow the routing as before, so the hit rate falls as the share grows past what the workload always routes

profile_save.description: a routing profile the plugin writes at close() (and save_profile()): the decode routing it counted, hottest first; the next open() starts the cache from it. Relative to the package

settings.description: a settings file in the package (crit plugins offload --out offload.json): its expert-offload options and slots override these

record_routes.description: keep the last this many decode routes on the device (routes(), and trace_path): the routing trace crit plugins offload --trace replays

trace_path.description: with record_routes, write the recorded routes there at every telemetry() call and when the engine closes

workers.description: the workers of the host's pool, which the CPU tier runs on (Core's, crit_plugins.host: one a process), when this plugin is the first to ask for it (-1: Core's plan, one per physical core but the service thread's)

pin.description: with workers: pin each worker of the host's pool to a physical core of its own (Linux)

max_tokens.description: the most tokens a decode call posts the CPU at once; a call of more tokens is a prompt chunk unless forward() says otherwise

round_rows.description: the rows of a captured round the cache counts reads and hits for
